label: lem:constant_diff_rearrangement
title: Constant difference rearrangement
statement: Let $F, G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. If $F(b) - G(b) = F(a) - G(a)$ and $G(a) = 0$, then $G(b) = F(b) - F(a)$.
proof: From $F(b) - G(b) = F(a) - G(a)$ we get $G(b) - G(a) = F(b) - F(a)$. Substituting $G(a) = 0$ gives $G(b) = F(b) - F(a)$.
